author: KarlOlofA
title: App root & header
before:
Title: App root & header
Kind: ui
Links: app-state, git-service, new-node, project-view, session-loop
Files:
  src/app.rs

Root component.
Resolves the working directory from argv[1] or the current dir, optionally opens a file from argv[2], provides AppState as context and starts the Claude session coroutine.
It reloads .workbench data when cwd or repo_version changes.
The header has the graph toggle, folder picker (rfd), model and cost badges, permission-mode selector, a branch picker and a New session button.
The branch picker shows the current branch and opens a filterable list of local and remote branches; picking one runs git switch (remote-only branches get a local tracking branch), and typing a new name offers to create it.
open_folder switches the working folder (used by the folder picker and the project view), and a project chip in the header jumps to the project that contains the open folder.

author: KarlOlofA
title: Self-updater
after:
Title: Self-updater
Kind: service
Links: app-state, install-tooling
Files:
  src/update.rs
  src/update_view.rs
  build.rs
  src/style.css

Checks on startup whether GitHub's main branch has commits that the running build lacks.
It compares the commit embedded at build time (build.rs) with main through the GitHub compare API using curl.
If main is ahead, a header button opens and lists the new commits.
Choosing Update fetches main into a private checkout under ~/.cache/workbench/source and builds it in the background.
Restart now runs that checkout's install script in a detached process and reopens the current folder.

Before building it checks for git, curl, cargo and, on Linux, make, a C compiler, pkg-config and the GUI libraries.

If the folder isn't a git checkout (a ZIP download), it offers to link it to the GitHub repo so the update check works, stashing any files that differ from main.

author: KarlOlofA
title: Graph canvas
before:
Title: Graph canvas
Kind: component
Links: app-state, ghost-branches, graph-model
Files:
  src/graph_view.rs

SVG and HTML node diagram with pan, zoom, fit-to-view, node dragging (saves the position) and link creation by clicking.
It highlights the active flow path and colours nodes by kind.
It always shows one network: the main graph or the module the user has opened.
Module attachment nodes are drawn with a double teal border, the module name and node count, and are marked edited when their module has pending changes; double-clicking one opens the module, and a breadcrumb bar leads back up.
The toolbar's + Module… menu creates a new module or attaches an existing one here.

after:
Title: Git service
Kind: service
Links: project-files
Files:
  src/git.rs

Thin wrapper over the git CLI: repo detection, current branch, branch listing, switching and creating branches, porcelain status, ls-files, pushing the current branch, and a diff against a base that includes untracked files.
It parses the output into FileDiff, Hunk and DiffLine values, and each hunk can be turned back into a patch.
For the node history it reads git log -p of the history file and maps each entry's uid to the commit, reachable from HEAD, that first added its line.

Bottom-panel tab that lists recorded node and module changes newest first as classic line diffs, with who made each change (you, a teammate, Claude, or outside Workbench) and when.
When one node is selected (or a module is open) it can filter to just that node's history, and Show jumps to the node.

Files:

Bottom-panel tab that lists recorded node and module changes newest first as classic line diffs, with who made each change (you, a teammate, Claude, or outside Workbench) and when.
When one node is selected (or a module is open) it can filter to just that node's history, and Show jumps to the node.
The node inspector links here with a History (n) button.
There is no clear action because the log is shared with the repo.
In a git repository the list is grouped against the git state: an Uncommitted section first, for entries not yet in a commit on this branch, then one section per commit (short hash, subject, author, time), newest first.
Each entry also carries an uncommitted or commit-hash tag.
